transport.text: The sculptures and murals stand outdoors in the city centre and can be seen around the clock.

data.best_text: June to August for the archipelago and bright evenings, December for the Christmas markets.
data.day_budget_note: Per person per day excluding flights: a share of a mid-range double room, food, local transport and one sight. A rough estimate.

stay.label: Weekend
stay.text: The Old Town, the Vasa Museum and a ferry across to Djurgården.

stay.label: Long weekend
stay.text: Time for Skansen, the metro art and half a day at Drottningholm.

stay.label: One week
stay.text: Add the archipelago with an overnight stay and quieter days on Södermalm.

areas.name: Södermalm
areas.text: The most restaurants and bars, views from the heights and the metro in every direction.

areas.name: Norrmalm and City
areas.text: Closest to the Central Station and the airport train. Practical but impersonal.

areas.name: Vasastan
areas.text: A quieter residential area with good food and walking distance to the city centre.

areas.name: Gamla stan (the Old Town)
areas.text: Beautiful to walk in but expensive and cramped to stay in. Visit during the day.

transport.text: Runs between Slussen and Djurgården via Skeppsholmen. SL cards are valid and single tickets can be bought on the quay.
The stations are decorated with art, so the ride is a sight in itself.

events.name: Stockholm International Film Festival
events.text: Screenings in cinemas all over the city.

events.name: Nobel Week Lights
events.text: Light installations in the city during Nobel Week. Free.

events.name: Lucia
events.text: Lucia processions in churches and at Skansen.

events.name: Stockholm Design Week
events.text: Exhibitions and open showrooms all over the city.

events.name: Stockholm Marathon
events.text: Start and finish at the Stadium. Hotels are more expensive that weekend and streets are closed.

month_notes: Cold and dark. Cheap to stay.
Winter. Sometimes ice to walk on.
Spring arrives and the cherry trees bloom in Kungsträdgården.
Green and bright. The archipelago boats start running more often.
Bright nights and Midsummer. Many people leave the city over the holiday.
Warmest. Swimming and the archipelago, but some restaurants are closed for the holidays.
Late summer and crayfish parties. Still swimming weather.
Clear autumn air and fewer tourists.
The darkest and greyest time, before Advent.
Christmas markets and Christmas buffets. Dark early.

prices.summary: Sweden's most expensive city, but the price level is familiar.
tips: A double room costs around 195 euros per night on average according to Kayak, roughly 2,150 kronor.

SE-fakta-systembolaget.title: Systembolaget from age 20
SE-fakta-systembolaget.body: The age limit at Systembolaget, the state alcohol shop, is 20. In restaurants and bars anyone aged 18 or over may buy alcohol.

SE-fakta-servering.title: Alcohol in bars from age 18
SE-fakta-servering.summary: Serving alcohol is permitted from age 18.
SE-fakta-servering.body: Parliament has set the age of majority, 18, as the limit for buying alcohol in restaurants. Individual venues may have a higher age limit at the door.

SE-fakta-systemet-tider.title: Systembolaget closes early
SE-fakta-systemet-tider.summary: Closes at 8 pm at the latest on weekdays and 3 pm on Saturdays. Closed on Sundays.
SE-fakta-systemet-tider.body: The shops close at 8 pm at the latest on weekdays and at 3 pm on Saturdays. They are closed on Sundays, public holidays, Christmas Eve and Midsummer Eve. Shop before the weekend.

SE-fakta-allemansratten.title: The right of public access: camp for a night or so
SE-fakta-allemansratten.summary: Do not disturb, do not destroy. Camping for the odd night is included.
SE-fakta-allemansratten.body: There is no law on how long you may camp in the same place, but the rule of thumb is a night or so with two or three tents. Do not disturb the landowner and do not damage nature. National parks and reserves have their own rules.

SE-fakta-varldsarv.title: 15 World Heritage Sites
SE-fakta-varldsarv.summary: Sweden has 15 World Heritage Sites, from Laponia to Karlskrona.
SE-fakta-varldsarv.body: The oldest Swedish World Heritage Site is Drottningholm from 1991 and the most recent is the Decorated Farmhouses of Hälsingland from 2012.

SE-fakta-nationalparker.title: First in Europe with national parks
SE-fakta-nationalparker.summary: The first nine national parks were established in 1909.
SE-fakta-nationalparker.body: Sweden established its first nine national parks in 1909 and was then first in Europe. They include Abisko, Sarek and Garphyttan.

SE-boras-fakta-pinocchio.title: Nine metres of Pinocchio
SE-boras-fakta-pinocchio.summary: Jim Dine's bronze sculpture Walking to Borås is nine metres tall.
SE-boras-fakta-pinocchio.body: The sculpture arrived in 2008 and was the start of Borås as a city of sculpture. The name is often associated with the knallar, the pedlars who walked the country selling textiles.

SE-boras-fakta-arenan.title: Elfsborg started as Borås Fotbollslag
SE-boras-fakta-arenan.summary: IF Elfsborg was founded on 26 June 1904 and has played at Borås Arena since 2005.
SE-boras-fakta-arenan.body: The club was formed as Borås Fotbollslag and is known as Di Gule. The first match at Borås Arena was played on 17 April 2005.

SE-stockholm-fakta-skansen.title: The world's oldest open-air museum
SE-stockholm-fakta-skansen.summary: Skansen on Djurgården was founded in 1891 by Artur Hazelius.
SE-stockholm-fakta-skansen.body: Skansen is regarded as the world's first open-air museum and is still on Djurgården.

SE-boras-walking-to-boras.name: Walking to Borås
SE-boras-walking-to-boras.summary: A nine-metre bronze Pinocchio by Jim Dine.
SE-boras-walking-to-boras.body: The city's most talked-about sculpture. A good starting point for a sculpture walk through the centre.

SE-boras-gatukonsten.name: The murals
SE-boras-gatukonsten.summary: Wall paintings the size of seven-storey buildings, left from No Limit Street Art.
SE-boras-gatukonsten.body: The festival started in 2014 and has merged with the sculpture biennial into Borås Art Biennial. The works are outdoors and free to see.

SE-boras-textilmuseet.name: The Textile Museum
SE-boras-textilmuseet.summary: Fashion and the textile industry in the Textile Fashion Center.
SE-boras-textilmuseet.body: Located at Skaraborgsvägen 3A in Simonsland, between the centre and Knalleland. Tickets are bought at the information desk outside the museum entrance.

SE-boras-djurparken.name: Borås Zoo
SE-boras-djurparken.summary: 40 hectares of African and Nordic animals in the middle of the city.
SE-boras-djurparken.body: The park has a savannah, bears, barbecue areas and playgrounds. Check the opening hours, they vary with the season.

SE-boras-abecita.name: Abecita Pop Art & Photo
SE-boras-abecita.summary: Around 500 works on three floors, including Warhol and Lichtenstein.
SE-boras-abecita.body: Located north of the Textile Fashion Center, towards Knalleland and the zoo.

SE-boras-konstmuseet.name: Borås Art Museum
SE-boras-konstmuseet.body: The museum leads the work on the city's new murals and organises Borås Art Biennial together with the Textile Museum.

SE-boras-arena.name: Borås Arena
SE-boras-arena.body: Watch Di Gule play at home. The arena is also used by Norrby IF.

SE-stockholm-vasamuseet.name: The Vasa Museum
SE-stockholm-vasamuseet.summary: Free admission up to and including age 18. Allow 90 minutes.
SE-stockholm-vasamuseet.body: The museum recommends 90 minutes for a visit. The adult price is higher May–September than the rest of the year.

SE-stockholm-skansen.name: Skansen
SE-stockholm-skansen.summary: The world's oldest open-air museum, founded in 1891.
SE-stockholm-skansen.body: Houses from all over the country and Nordic animals on Djurgården.

SE-stockholm-djurgardsfarjan.name: The Djurgården ferry
SE-stockholm-djurgardsfarjan.body: The nicest way to Djurgården. SL cards are valid, and single tickets can be bought on the quay.

SE-stockholm-tunnelbanekonsten.name: The art in the metro
SE-stockholm-tunnelbanekonsten.summary: Called the world's longest art exhibition.
SE-stockholm-tunnelbanekonsten.body: More than 150 artists have contributed. Tekniska högskolan station won a national architecture prize in 1973.

SE-stockholm-drottningholm.name: Drottningholm
SE-stockholm-drottningholm.body: A royal palace on the French model, with the Chinese Pavilion and the palace theatre.

SE-stockholm-skogskyrkogarden.name: Skogskyrkogården (the Woodland Cemetery)
SE-stockholm-skogskyrkogarden.body: Regarded as one of the great works of modern architecture. Located in southern Stockholm.

SE-uppland-birka.name: Birka and Hovgården
SE-uppland-birka.summary: A Viking town in Lake Mälaren, a World Heritage Site since 1993.
SE-uppland-birka.body: A trading place with far-reaching contacts in the 8th and 9th centuries.

SE-sodermanland-tyresta.name: Tyresta National Park
SE-sodermanland-tyresta.summary: A national park since 1993 in Haninge and Tyresö.
SE-sodermanland-tyresta.body: 1,964 hectares of forest just south of Stockholm.

SE-lappland-laponia.name: Laponia
SE-lappland-laponia.summary: A World Heritage Site since 1996 and a Sami cultural landscape.
SE-lappland-laponia.body: Vast and remote wilderness that is also the cultural landscape of the Sami.

SE-lappland-abisko.name: Abisko National Park
SE-lappland-abisko.summary: One of the first nine national parks, 1909.
SE-lappland-abisko.body: 7,700 hectares south of Lake Torneträsk in Kiruna municipality.

SE-lappland-sarek.name: Sarek
SE-lappland-sarek.summary: 197,000 hectares of mountains without trails, a national park since 1909.
SE-lappland-sarek.body: Located in Jokkmokk municipality. For experienced mountain hikers.

SE-norrbotten-gammelstad.name: Gammelstad Church Town
SE-norrbotten-gammelstad.summary: Around 400 church cottages, a World Heritage Site since 1996.
SE-norrbotten-gammelstad.body: The cottages were only used at church festivals and holidays.

SE-norrbotten-haparanda-skargard.name: Haparanda Archipelago
SE-norrbotten-haparanda-skargard.summary: A national park since 1995 in the Bothnian Bay.
SE-norrbotten-haparanda-skargard.body: 6,000 hectares of archipelago south of Haparanda and Kalix.

SE-angermanland-hoga-kusten.name: The High Coast
SE-angermanland-hoga-kusten.summary: A World Heritage Site since 2000, shaped by ice and land uplift.
SE-angermanland-hoga-kusten.body: Here you can clearly see how the ice sheet, the rapid land uplift and the waves have shaped the landscape.

SE-angermanland-skuleskogen.name: Skuleskogen National Park
SE-angermanland-skuleskogen.summary: A national park since 1984 in Örnsköldsvik and Kramfors.
SE-angermanland-skuleskogen.body: 3,062 hectares in the middle of the High Coast.

SE-halsingland-halsingegardar.name: The Decorated Farmhouses of Hälsingland
SE-halsingland-halsingegardar.summary: Richly decorated farmhouses, a World Heritage Site since 2012.
SE-halsingland-halsingegardar.body: The farms' festive rooms are the high point of a long building tradition among the farmers.

SE-dalarna-falu-gruva.name: Falun and the Great Copper Mountain
SE-dalarna-falu-gruva.summary: The Great Copper Mountain, a World Heritage Site since 2001.
SE-dalarna-falu-gruva.body: The mine and the district around it are a rare reminder of early Swedish industry.

SE-dalarna-fulufjallet.name: Fulufjället National Park
SE-dalarna-fulufjallet.summary: 38,500 hectares of mountains in Älvdalen, a national park since 2002.

SE-vastmanland-engelsberg.name: Engelsberg Ironworks
SE-vastmanland-engelsberg.summary: A well-preserved ironworks, a World Heritage Site since 1993.
SE-vastmanland-engelsberg.body: Buildings and installations remain as they were.

SE-gastrikland-farnebofjarden.name: Färnebofjärden National Park
SE-gastrikland-farnebofjarden.summary: A national park since 1998 by the Dalälven river.
SE-gastrikland-farnebofjarden.body: 10,100 hectares, of which 4,110 are water, shared between the counties of Västmanland, Dalarna and Gävleborg.

SE-bohuslan-tanum.name: The rock carvings in Tanum
SE-bohuslan-tanum.summary: Europe's largest collection of Bronze Age rock carvings.

SE-bohuslan-kosterhavet.name: Kosterhavet
SE-bohuslan-kosterhavet.body: 38,878 hectares in northern Bohuslän, 98 per cent of it water.

SE-gotland-visby.name: The Hanseatic Town of Visby

SE-gotland-visby.body: A medieval Hanseatic town with small-scale buildings inside the wall.

SE-gotland-gotska-sandon.name: Gotska Sandön
SE-gotland-gotska-sandon.body: 4,490 hectares of island and sea north of Gotland.

SE-halland-grimeton.name: The Grimeton Radio Station

SE-angermanland-landskapsdjur.summary: The beaver is the provincial animal of Ångermanland.
SE-angermanland-landskapsdjur.body: Tick it off when you have seen the animal in Ångermanland.

SE-angermanland-landskapsblomma.summary: Wild pansy is the provincial flower of Ångermanland.
SE-angermanland-landskapsblomma.body: Tick it off when you have found it in Ångermanland.

SE-oland-landskapsdjur.summary: The thrush nightingale is the provincial animal of Öland.
SE-oland-landskapsdjur.body: Tick it off when you have seen the animal on Öland.

SE-oland-landskapsblomma.name: Provincial flower: Öland rock rose
SE-oland-landskapsblomma.summary: Öland rock rose is the provincial flower of Öland.
SE-oland-landskapsblomma.body: Tick it off when you have found it on Öland.

SE-ostergotland-landskapsdjur.name: Provincial animal: Mute swan
SE-ostergotland-landskapsdjur.summary: The mute swan is the provincial animal of Östergötland.
SE-ostergotland-landskapsdjur.body: Tick it off when you have seen the animal in Östergötland.

SE-ostergotland-landskapsblomma.summary: Cornflower is the provincial flower of Östergötland.
SE-ostergotland-landskapsblomma.body: Tick it off when you have found it in Östergötland.

SE-ostergotland-bergs-slussar.name: The Berg locks
SE-ostergotland-bergs-slussar.summary: Seven connected locks lift the boats 18.8 metres from Lake Roxen.
SE-ostergotland-bergs-slussar.body: The Carl Johan flight of locks is part of the Göta Canal, which is 190 km long and has 58 locks. Walk or cycle along the car-free towpath.

SE-varmland-marbacka.name: Mårbacka
SE-varmland-marbacka.summary: Selma Lagerlöf's childhood home in Sunne municipality.
SE-varmland-marbacka.body: The first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature was born and grew up here. The estate is shown as a memorial home.

SE-medelpad-stenstaden.name: The Stone City in Sundsvall
SE-medelpad-stenstaden.summary: Lavish stone buildings built after the city fire of 1888.
SE-medelpad-stenstaden.body: On a June day in 1888 most of Sundsvall burned down. The city was rebuilt in stone, and Hotel Knaust from 1891 still receives guests.

SE-jamtland-tannforsen.name: Tännforsen
SE-jamtland-tannforsen.summary: Sweden's largest unregulated waterfall, with a drop of 37 metres.
SE-jamtland-tannforsen.body: A nature reserve in Åre municipality, about 15 km north-west of Duved. The path can be icy in winter.

SE-vasterbotten-vasterbottensost.name: Västerbotten cheese in Burträsk
SE-vasterbotten-vasterbottensost.summary: The cheese is only made in Burträsk, for the first time in 1872.
SE-vasterbotten-vasterbottensost.body: The visitor centre is by the dairy and has an exhibition and a shop. The recipe was created by the dairymaid Ulrika Eleonora Lindström.

sevardhet-pinocchio-boras.name: Walking to Borås
sevardhet-pinocchio-boras.hint: Nine metres of bronze with a long nose.

SE-boras-skulpturpromenad.title: Sculpture walk through the centre
SE-boras-skulpturpromenad.body: Start at Pinocchio and walk towards the Textile Fashion Center. Count how many sculptures you find on the way.

SE-boras-muraljakt.title: Mural hunt
SE-boras-muraljakt.body: Find the biggest wall paintings in the city and photograph your favourite.

SE-boras-museidag.title: Two museums in one afternoon
SE-boras-museidag.body: The Art Museum always has free admission. Take the Textile Museum or Abecita afterwards.

SE-boras-djurparken-matsack.title: The zoo with a packed lunch
SE-boras-djurparken-matsack.body: Walk around the savannah and barbecue at one of the barbecue areas.

SE-boras-elfsborg.title: Elfsborg at home
SE-boras-elfsborg.body: Watch a match at Borås Arena.

SE-boras-grimeton.title: World Heritage in Grimeton and the sea in Varberg
SE-boras-grimeton.body: Visit the radio station in Grimeton and finish by the sea in Varberg.

SE-boras-store-mosse.title: Boardwalk hike at Store Mosse
SE-boras-store-mosse.body: A national park in Småland with a walk across the bog.

SE-boras-tiveden.title: Tiveden National Park
SE-boras-tiveden.body: A forest hike in the national park on the border with Närke.

SE-stockholm-djurgardsdag.title: A Djurgården day by boat
SE-stockholm-djurgardsdag.body: Take the Djurgården ferry from Slussen, visit the Vasa Museum and continue to Skansen.

SE-stockholm-tunnelbanekonst.title: Art tour in the metro
SE-stockholm-tunnelbanekonst.body: Choose three stations and get off at each. Works in any weather.

SE-stockholm-skogskyrkogarden-promenad.title: A walk in Skogskyrkogården
SE-stockholm-skogskyrkogarden-promenad.body: A quiet walk in a World Heritage Site.

SE-stockholm-drottningholm-utflykt.title: Drottningholm
SE-stockholm-drottningholm-utflykt.body: The palace park, the Chinese Pavilion and the palace theatre on the same outing.

SE-stockholm-tyresta.title: Tyresta National Park
SE-stockholm-tyresta.body: A forest hike just south of the city.

SE-stockholm-helg.title: Stockholm over the weekend
SE-stockholm-helg.body: One day on Djurgården and one day with metro art and Skogskyrkogården or Drottningholm.

SE-hemma-nasta-resa.title: Plan the next trip
SE-hemma-nasta-resa.body: Open the map, choose a country each and compare what appeals most.

SE-hemma-laga-ett-land.title: Cook a country
SE-hemma-laga-ett-land.body: Choose a country from the bucket list and cook a dish from there.

SE-hemma-bucketlistkvall.title: Bucket list evening
SE-hemma-bucketlistkvall.body: Swipe through the suggestions separately and see where you match.

SE-hemma-filmmaraton.title: Themed movie marathon
SE-hemma-filmmaraton.body: Choose a director, a country or a decade and watch two films in a row. Whoever did not choose the films chooses the snacks.

SE-hemma-blindtest.title: Blind test
SE-hemma-blindtest.body: Buy three kinds of the same thing, for example chocolate or soda, and guess which is which. The loser does the dishes.

SE-hemma-ny-ratt.title: Cook something neither of you has cooked
SE-hemma-ny-ratt.body: Choose a recipe that feels a little too hard and cook it together from start to finish.

SE-hemma-pizza-fran-grunden.title: Pizza from scratch
SE-hemma-pizza-fran-grunden.body: Make the dough in the morning and let it rest. In the evening you each make a pizza and vote for the winner.

SE-hemma-spelturnering.title: Game tournament
SE-hemma-spelturnering.body: Three different games, best of three. Decide the prize before you start.

SE-hemma-pussel.title: Jigsaw and podcast
SE-hemma-pussel.body: Do a big jigsaw and listen to a podcast or an audiobook meanwhile.

SE-hemma-fotokvall.title: Go through the year's photos
SE-hemma-fotokvall.body: Pick the ten best photos of the year and order them as real prints.

SE-hemma-koja.title: Build a blanket fort
SE-hemma-koja.body: Blankets, cushions and a string of lights in the living room. Eat dinner in there.

SE-hemma-fragor.title: Questions you never ask
SE-hemma-fragor.body: Ask each other questions you never usually ask. The phones stay in another room.

SE-hemma-spellista.title: Make a playlist for each other
SE-hemma-spellista.body: Ten songs each that the other has not heard. Listen through both and explain why you chose them.

SE-hemma-baka.title: Bake something new
SE-hemma-baka.body: Choose a pastry from a country you want to travel to and bake it at home.

SE-hemma-spakvall.title: Spa evening at home
SE-hemma-spakvall.body: Face mask, foot bath and candles. Turn off all screens.

SE-hemma-dromresan.title: Plan the dream trip for real
SE-hemma-dromresan.body: Choose a destination and work out flights, accommodation and days as if you were booking tomorrow.

SE-hemma-brev.title: Write letters to yourselves
SE-hemma-brev.body: Each write a letter to be opened in a year. Put them in an envelope with the date on it.

SE-hemma-teckna.title: Draw each other
SE-hemma-teckna.body: Five minutes per portrait, without looking at the paper. Put the result up on the fridge.

SE-hemma-sprakkvall.title: Language evening
SE-hemma-sprakkvall.body: Teach each other twenty words in a language the other does not know. Test each other the next day.

SE-hemma-frukost-middag.title: Breakfast for dinner
SE-hemma-frukost-middag.body: Pancakes, eggs and freshly squeezed juice at seven in the evening.

SE-hemma-rensa.title: Clear out a wardrobe together
SE-hemma-rensa.body: Try everything on, keep what gets used and donate the rest. Finish with something nice to eat.

SE-ut-solnedgang.title: Sunset with a thermos
SE-ut-solnedgang.body: Find the nearest hill or jetty with a view to the west and bring something warm to drink.

SE-ut-ny-vag.title: Walk a route you have never walked
SE-ut-ny-vag.body: Turn the other way outside the door and keep going for half an hour. Take a different way home.

SE-ut-fika-ute.title: Fika outdoors
SE-ut-fika-ute.body: Buy coffee and something sweet and sit in a park instead of a café. Works all year with the right clothes.

SE-ut-fotopromenad.title: Photo walk
SE-ut-fotopromenad.body: Choose a theme, for example doors or signs, and take ten photos each. Compare when you get home.

SE-ut-loppis.title: Flea market round
SE-ut-loppis.body: Give each other fifty kronor and buy a present for the other at a flea market or second-hand shop.

SE-ut-stjarnor.title: Stargazing
SE-ut-stjarnor.body: Travel a little way out from the city lights on a clear evening. Bring a blanket and something warm.

SE-ut-turist-hemma.title: Be tourists in your own city
SE-ut-turist-hemma.body: Do the things you would recommend to a visitor but have never done yourselves.

SE-ut-slumpbuss.title: Take a bus to the last stop
SE-ut-slumpbuss.body: Get on a line you never ride and see what is at the far end.

SE-present-dalahast.name: Dala horse
SE-present-dalahast.body: The painted wooden horse from Dalarna. Choose a small one that fits in hand luggage.

SE-present-polkagrisar.name: Polkagris candy canes from Gränna
SE-present-polkagrisar.body: Red and white peppermint sticks. They keep for a long time and survive packing.

SE-present-knackebrod.name: Crispbread in a round
SE-present-knackebrod.body: The large round with a hole in the middle. Light, cheap and looks Swedish.

SE-present-lakrits.name: Salty liquorice
SE-present-lakrits.body: A good gift for someone who already likes it, and a fun test for someone who has never tried it.

SE-present-hjortronsylt.name: Cloudberry jam
SE-present-hjortronsylt.body: Berries from the bogs in the north. A glass jar, so pack it in checked baggage.

SE-present-tramugg.name: Wooden kåsa
SE-present-tramugg.body: A drinking cup with a handle for coffee outdoors. Comes in both wood and plastic for hiking.

SE-present-glas.name: Glass from the Kingdom of Crystal
SE-present-glas.body: Hand-blown glass from the glassworks in Småland. Buy something small, for example a tealight holder.

SE-present-lovikka.name: Lovikka mittens
SE-present-lovikka.body: Thick wool mittens with a coloured tassel, from Lovikka in Norrbotten.
